newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards inch up.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards inch up.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.60/61 on Friday compared with the opening quote of 35.59/61, dealers said.
They said the market saw little action in the absence of any major demand for dollars. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) continued to mop up dollars, preventing the rupee's rise.
Some profit-booking in the foward dollar market saw the premia edge up, with six month premia closing at 7.13 percent, up from 6.97 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
They said the sharp fall in yield at Friday's 91-day treasury bills auction to 8.86 percent from 10.07 percent provided fresh evidence of RBI's determination to bring down interest rates.

The RBI announced a package of measures to bring down interest rates on October 19. The first phase of a cut in cash reserve ratio (CRR) scheduled for October 26 will release about 20 billion rupees into the banking system.
"It (six month premium) could dip to about 6.0 percent," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay.
